epithet: The rights of those who could not claim them
lede: Uḥud had left Madinah full of widows and orphans, in a society where a woman did not inherit and could herself be inherited. Into that came a surah that names the daughter’s share, the wife’s share and the mother’s share in exact fractions, and tells the guardian of an orphan that what he swallows of the child’s property is fire.

names.name: al-Nisāʾ
names.note: For how much of it legislates for women — their inheritance, their dowries, their marriages, their protection. It is the longer “surah of women”; Ibn Masʿūd called Sūrat al-Ṭalāq the shorter one.

revelation.detail: A few reports call it Makkan, and al-Qurṭubī sets them aside on two grounds. ʿĀʾishah said that Sūrat al-Nisāʾ came down only when she was already in the Prophet’s household, and there is no dispute that he married her in Madinah; and anyone who looks at its rulings knows it to be Madinan beyond doubt. One ayah — “Allah commands you to render trusts to those to whom they are due” — is related to the day Makkah was conquered and the keys of the Kaʿbah, and what was revealed after the Hijrah is Madinan wherever it came down. Its last ayah is, by al-Barāʾ’s report, the last ayah of the Qurʾan to be revealed. The traditional order places it ninety-second.
revelation.when: Madinah, in the years after Uḥud — with ayat added as late as the last

evidence.quote: فَإِنَّ فِي صَحِيحِ الْبُخَارِيِّ عَنْ عَائِشَةَ أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ: مَا نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ النِّسَاءِ إِلَّا وَأَنَا عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، تَعْنِي قَدْ بَنَى بِهَا
وَمَنْ تَبَيَّنَ أَحْكَامَهَا عَلِمَ أَنَّهَا مَدَنِيَّةٌ لَا شَكَّ فِيهَا
قَالَ العَوْفِي عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: نَزَلَتْ سورةُ النِّسَاءِ بِالْمَدِينَةِ

setting: It opens by going back to the beginning: “O mankind, be mindful of your Lord, who created you from a single soul, and created from it its mate, and spread from the two of them many men and women.” Everything the surah goes on to legislate rests on that sentence. The orphan, the woman, the slave, the stranger and the man of standing come from one soul.

Then it turns at once to the people the old order left out. Before Islam, inheritance went to the men who could ride and fight; women and small children received nothing. Ibn ʿAbbās relates that when a man died, his heirs had the best claim to his widow: one of them might marry her if he wished, or they might marry her off, or refuse to let her marry at all. ʿĀʾishah explains the surah’s third ayah as being about the orphan girl in her guardian’s care, whose property and beauty he likes, and whom he means to marry without giving her what another would have to give.

The answer came, in one case, to a man lying unconscious. Jābir said: the Prophet ﷺ and Abū Bakr came on foot to visit me among Banū Salimah, and found me insensible. He called for water, made ablution and sprinkled some of it on me, and I came to. I said: what do you command me to do with my property, Messenger of Allah? And there came down: “Allah charges you concerning your children: for the male, the like of the share of two females…” — and then the fractions, one after another: a half, a quarter, an eighth, two-thirds, a third, a sixth. “These are the limits of Allah.”

The second half of the surah widens from the household to the city. It deals with the hypocrites who turned back on the road to Uḥud; with obedience and its limit — “obey Allah, and obey the Messenger, and those in authority among you; and if you dispute about anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger”; with fighting for the sake of the men, women and children who are held down and cry out for a protector; with the prayer of an army in the face of the enemy; and with justice, which it demands in the hardest form there is: “Be upholders of justice, witnesses for Allah, even against yourselves, or your parents and kin.”

It ends with the People of the Book — the claim that the Messiah was killed, and the claim that he was more than a messenger — and then, as its very last ayah, returns to where it began: one more rule of inheritance.

occasions.title: The orphan girl and her guardian
occasions.text: ʿUrwah asked ʿĀʾishah about “If you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans.” She said: “Son of my sister, this is the orphan girl who is in the care of her guardian and shares his property; her wealth and beauty please him, and he wishes to marry her without being fair in her dowry and giving her what another would give. So they were forbidden to marry them unless they dealt justly with them and gave them the highest of what is customary in dowry.”

occasions.title: The ayah of the shares
occasions.text: Jābir said: “The Prophet ﷺ and Abū Bakr visited me among Banū Salimah, walking. The Prophet ﷺ found me unconscious; he called for water, made ablution from it, then sprinkled it upon me, and I came round. I said: ‘What do you command me to do with my wealth, Messenger of Allah?’ And there came down: ‘Allah charges you concerning your children.’”
occasions.source: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: al-Bukhārī (4577) and Muslim (1616).

occasions.title: Women inherited against their will
occasions.text: “When a man died, his heirs had more right to his wife. If one of them wished, he married her; if they wished, they gave her in marriage; and if they wished, they did not. They had more right to her than her own family. So this ayah came down about that.”

occasions.title: “Until they make you judge”
occasions.text: Al-Zubayr disputed with a man of the Helpers over a watercourse in the lava field. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Water your land, Zubayr, then let the water run to your neighbour.” The man said: “Is it because he is your cousin, Messenger of Allah?” His face changed, and he said: “Water, Zubayr, then hold the water until it reaches the walls.” Al-Zubayr said: “I think these ayat came down only about that: ‘No, by your Lord, they do not believe until they make you judge in what is disputed among them.’”
occasions.source: ʿUrwah, from al-Zubayr: al-Bukhārī (4585) and Muslim (2357).

occasions.title: The man who gave the greeting
occasions.text: “A man was with a small flock of his, and the Muslims came upon him. He said: ‘Peace be upon you.’ They killed him and took his flock. So Allah sent down: ‘Do not say to one who offers you peace, “You are not a believer,” seeking the goods of this life.’”

occasions.title: “Other than those with an injury”
occasions.text: Zayd ibn Thābit said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dictated to him: “Not equal are those of the believers who sit and those who strive in the way of Allah.” Ibn Umm Maktūm came while he was dictating it and said: “Messenger of Allah, by Allah, if I were able to strive, I would” — and he was blind. So Allah sent down upon His Messenger ﷺ, while his thigh was upon mine, and it grew so heavy on me that I feared my thigh would be crushed. Then it lifted from him, and Allah had sent down: “other than those with an injury.”

aim: To order the Muslim community from within, by safeguarding social and financial rights — clearing away what remained of the Age of Ignorance, and centring on the rights of women and the weak.

outline.title: One soul; orphans; the shares
outline.summary: O mankind, be mindful of your Lord, who created you from a single soul. Give the orphans their property. Give the women their dowries as a free gift. For men is a share of what parents and near kin leave, and for women is a share — be it little or much. Those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only swallowing fire into their bellies. Allah charges you concerning your children: for the male, the like of the share of two females… for parents, a sixth each… for you, half of what your wives leave… These are the limits of Allah.

outline.title: Protections for women
outline.summary: Repentance is accepted by Allah only from those who do wrong in ignorance and then repent soon. O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will. Live with them honourably: if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing in which Allah has placed much good. How could you take it back, when you have gone in to one another? Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters… Allah wishes to lighten things for you; and man was created weak.

outline.title: Property, the household, and the neighbour
outline.summary: Do not consume one another’s wealth wrongfully, and do not kill yourselves. If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We shall remit your lesser misdeeds. Men are the maintainers of women. If you fear a breach between the two, appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from hers. Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him; and be good to parents, kin, orphans, the needy, the near neighbour and the distant. Allah does not wrong by so much as an atom’s weight. How will it be when We bring from every community a witness, and bring you as a witness over these? (4:41)

outline.title: Trusts, judgement and obedience
outline.summary: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, purchasing error? Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, and He forgives what is less than that to whom He wills. Allah commands you to render trusts to those to whom they are due, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Obey Allah, and obey the Messenger, and those in authority among you. No, by your Lord, they do not believe until they make you judge in what is disputed among them. Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger will be with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous.

outline.title: Fighting, emigration and the prayer of fear
outline.summary: O you who believe, take your precaution. Why should you not fight in the way of Allah, and for the oppressed men, women and children who say, “Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers”? Wherever you are, death will overtake you. Do they not ponder the Qurʾan? When you are greeted, return a better greeting. A believer does not kill a believer, except by mistake. When you go out in the way of Allah, verify. Those whom the angels take while wronging themselves: “Was Allah’s earth not wide enough for you to emigrate?” When you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a party of them stand with you.

outline.title: Do not plead for the treacherous
outline.summary: We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you; do not be an advocate for the treacherous. Whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks Allah’s forgiveness will find Allah forgiving and merciful. Whoever earns a fault and then casts it on an innocent has taken on slander. There is no good in much of their private talk, except one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation. Who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah and follows the way of Ibrāhīm?

outline.title: Justice within the house, and the hypocrites
outline.summary: They ask you for a ruling about women. If a woman fears ill-treatment or desertion from her husband, there is no blame on them if they come to terms; and reconciliation is best. O you who believe, be upholders of justice, witnesses for Allah, even against yourselves (4:135). Give the hypocrites the news of a painful punishment: those who wait upon you; who stand for prayer lazily, to be seen by people. The hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire — except those who repent.

outline.title: The People of the Book, and the last ruling
outline.summary: The People of the Book ask you to bring down upon them a book from heaven. For their breaking of the covenant, and their saying, “We killed the Messiah” — they did not kill him, nor crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them; rather, Allah raised him to Himself. We have revealed to you as We revealed to Nūḥ and the prophets after him. People of the Book, do not go to excess in your religion: the Messiah, ʿĪsā son of Maryam, was only a messenger of Allah. Do not say “Three.” They ask you for a ruling: say, Allah gives you a ruling about one who leaves neither parent nor child.

keyAyah.why: The standard the whole surah applies — to the guardian, the husband, the judge and the witness: justice that does not bend for oneself or one’s own.

virtues.text: Ibn Masʿūd said: The Prophet ﷺ said to me: “Recite to me.” I said: “Shall I recite to you, when it was sent down to you?” He said: “I love to hear it from someone else.” So I recited Sūrat al-Nisāʾ to him until I reached: “How will it be when We bring from every community a witness, and bring you as a witness over these?” He said: “Enough.” And his eyes were streaming.

Ibn Masʿūd said: “In Sūrat al-Nisāʾ there are five ayat for which I would not be glad to have this world and all that is in it”: that Allah does not wrong by an atom’s weight (4:40); that if you avoid the major sins, the lesser are remitted (4:31); that Allah forgives what is less than idolatry to whom He wills (4:48); “had they, when they wronged themselves, come to you” (4:64); and “whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks Allah’s forgiveness, will find Allah forgiving and merciful” (4:110).
virtues.source: Al-Ḥākim, al-Mustadrak — quoted by Ibn Kathīr
virtues.grade: Al-Ḥākim: a sound chain, if ʿAbd al-Raḥmān heard it from his father Ibn Masʿūd — which is disputed

evidence.quote: قَالَ: إِنَّ فِي سُورَةِ النِّسَاءِ لخمسُ آيَاتٍ مَا يَسُرّني أَنَّ لِي بِهَا الدُّنْيَا وَمَا فِيهَا

virtues.text: Al-Barāʾ said: “The last surah to come down was Barāʾah, and the last ayah to come down was: ‘They ask you for a ruling…’” — the closing ayah of al-Nisāʾ.

before: Āl ʿImrān closed: “be mindful of Allah, that you may succeed.” Al-Nisāʾ opens with the same command, addressed now to all mankind, and grounds it in their common origin.
after: Al-Nisāʾ sets out the bonds of kinship, marriage and inheritance. Al-Māʾidah begins: “O you who believe, fulfil your contracts.”

notable.label: The ayah of the ten rights
What Allah does not forgive, and what He does
Render the trusts; judge with justice
For the oppressed men, women and children
Whoever seeks forgiveness will find it
“They did not kill him, nor crucify him”
Do not go to excess in your religion

sources: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; al-Ḥākim, al-Mustadrak
